audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The exclusion (phrasal iambic metre, no word-level stress; StressTyp2's second-syllable coding rejected) rests on the best available source, Reesink's 1999 reference grammar, whose dedicated metrical-stress section (pp.32-39) states exactly this and is held and verified verbatim at p.32 and p.39. Donohue 1997, downloaded now, is silent on stress placement and does not disturb the classification. Only bookkeeping is suggested: populate quote/cite/loc/grade from the copy we hold (Reesink 1999:32, section 2.10; grade page-read) instead of leaving them empty with the quotation only in the contra note, and repair the truncated second contra sentence. no reclassification.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1997. Hatam phonology and grammatical notes. In Andrew Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 3, 37-57. Pacific Linguistics A-87. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: No word-stress rule is stated. Stress is invoked only as a diagnostic for epenthetic vs phonemic vowels: 'The stress is noticeably stronger on words containing [ɛ], [a] or [ɔ] than [i] or [u]' (p.44); transcriptions such as /pketa/ [pə'gɛda] show stress never on the epenthetic schwa, consistent with Reesink's 'weak syllable never stressed'.
sources.locator: section 2.4, p.44 (only stress mention); sections 2.1-2.5 contain no stress-placement rule
sources.note: Only other published phonology of Hatam; checked for an independent stress statement (none; silent).
